title: No Shortcuts to Culture: Indonesian Multi-hop Question Answering for Complex Cultural Understanding

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model performance on a culturally grounded multi-hop QA dataset (ID-MoCQA) and performing qualitative error analysis to identify systematic preferences for dominant, prominent, or widely documented cultural practices over correct region-specific local customs.

Qualitative analysis of incorrect QA responses to observe instances where models inappropriately apply majority religious frameworks (e.g., Islamic mourning traditions) to contexts involving minority religious groups (e.g., Batak Christian practices).
Analyzing systematic QA failures where models incorrectly apply widespread patriarchal norms (e.g., the groom's family paying a dowry) to queries specifically involving matrilineal societies.

Examining model errors regarding indigenous and regional practices to detect reliance on generalized stereotypes (e.g., assuming 'traditional' implies 'communal sharing' for Papuan cultures) rather than factual, localized economic practices.
